info.name: Credential Service
info.description:
Team 16 - Student ID, please. Credential Service owns the documents an applicant presents and each document's validation status.

Lab 4: in the running system every request reaches the service through the Message Broker, on its queue requests.credential, and the events travel through the broker too. The broker speaks gRPC, which this collection cannot, so the folders below call the REST port directly - the same router the broker's requests are dispatched to - and 'Through the Gateway' shows the one player route that stays. scripts/mock-event.sh publishes a peer's event through the broker.

Run the folders in order: 'Contract endpoints' stores an applicant_id that the later folders reuse. Set base_url to wherever the service is listening (8082 by default).

The single most important assertion in here is in 'Documents (what players see)': the player-facing endpoint must never return validation_status or problems.

request.description: Says the process is serving. It deliberately checks no dependency: restarting a healthy container because somebody else's database was slow would be wrong.

Reports whether the service can do useful work. The database is the only hard dependency. `components.event_relay` says whether applicant.initialized can be pushed at all, and `consumers.<name>` how many deliveries still wait for each consumer (`pending`) or were refused with 422 (`parked`).

item.name: Through the Gateway
item.description: Lab 4: the Gateway forwards only the routes a player uses (CPR README "Gateway"); every other route of this service answers 404 there, and the services reach it through the Message Broker instead. For this service one route stays: GET /api/v1/credential/applicants/{id}/documents, with a player's `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`, which this folder's pre-request script mints for `player_id` with `jwt_secret`. The Gateway hands it to the broker, which delivers it to the least loaded instance; the service sees `X-Player-Id` and no credential. `GET /api/v1/credential/health` stays public. The validation - the answer key - is no Gateway route at all.

exec: // Player tokens, signed the way Player Service signs them: HS256 with JWT_SECRET, `sub` = the
// player's id, `iat` and `exp`. The Gateway verifies the signature, so `jwt_secret` must be the
// JWT_SECRET of the Gateway being called (gateway-service/.env).
return header + '.' + payload + '.' + b64url(CryptoJS.HmacSHA256(header + '.' + payload, secret));
pm.collectionVariables.set('player_token', mint({ sub: sub, iat: now, exp: now + 3600 }, secret));

request.description: `/api/v1/credential/health` is forwarded to the service's `/health`: a public route, no credential, not counted as a task. The Gateway adds `X-Request-ID` when the caller sent none.

item.name: Lab 3: status and Service Discovery
item.description: Lab 3: several copies of the service share one database, register themselves with Service Discovery and report their load on GET /status. Logs are JSON lines carrying `instance_id` and `request_id`, so `docker compose logs credential-service` shows which copy answered each request.

request.description: GET /status at the root, next to /health: this instance's health and load, in the shape every Lab 3 component shares. Service Discovery calls it directly, not through the Gateway, every 10 s with a 2 s timeout. No credential, and it is outside the concurrent task limit, so a saturated instance answers it (busy) instead of refusing it with a 429 (broken). 200 `up`, or 503 `degraded` with the same body when the database does not answer. `in_flight` / `max_concurrent_tasks` is the load; Service Discovery alerts at 80 %. This request calls this instance directly.

exec: pm.test('200 OK, or 503 when the database is down', () => pm.expect([200, 503]).to.include(pm.response.code));
pm.test('service is the Gateway prefix, instance_id is credential-<hostname>', () => {
pm.test('in_flight is a count within the limit', () => {

item.name: Status is not routed through the Gateway

request.description: Lab 4: the Gateway forwards only player routes, so /status - for Service Discovery inside the network - answers 404 there.

Every copy of the service registers itself with Service Discovery (PUT /api/v1/instances/{instance_id}) right after its listener is up and repeats it every 5 s; a copy that stops deregisters (DELETE). This is the list the Gateway reads every 5 s to share requests round-robin: `up` instances only. Needs Service Discovery (published on 8090 in the team stack). With `docker compose up -d --scale credential-service=3` it lists three.
